messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a p99 per-token latency spike in the EU fleet starting ~12:05 UTC, looks correlated with increased cross-region egress churn. panel: /dashboards/token-latency -> p99 jumped from 220ms -> 1.2s  :rotating_light:
jon: saw that too, grafana alert fired. Did we have any recent routing changes or peering flaps?
lee: net infra reported a transient BGP flap around 12:02, then some pod restarts on gpufleet-eu-west2. Could be node churn causing KV cache warmups and tail latency.
arun: cpu/network ops: there were 3 NAT gateway failovers for the region, plus a short spike of retransmits. Hop count to redis-caches increased for some shards.
maria: important: the p99 panel is an aggregate across all shards using histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)). I think summing across shards is exaggerating p99 — we saw double-sampling during node churn.
jon: ah, that would make sense. histogram_quantile over a sum loses shard boundaries. We probably need per-shard quantiles then take the max.
lee: quick proposal for recording rule + panel change:
```
# prometheus recording rule (rules/gpu-token.rules):
- record: job:token_latency:histogram_agg_per_shard
  expr: sum by(job, shard, le)(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m]))
- record: job:token_latency:histogram_quantile_shard
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, job:token_latency:histogram_agg_per_shard)
```
Then panel: show max(job:token_latency:histogram_quantile_shard) by (region) for p99.
maria: that should avoid the false-high p99 during partial outages. Also add an annotation for tokens/sec drops so we can see load vs latency.
arun: for mitigation I routed a subset of heavy customers to dedicated-reserve-eu-1 to reduce cross-region fallbacks. That cut p99 for routed traffic back to ~250ms. Cost hit ~3% of reserved pool for 2 hours.
jon: can we automate fallback to dedicated in the routing policy when cross-region retransmit rate > threshold?
lee: yes, we already have smart-routing rules, just need a new condition based on net_retransmits_rate or conn_errors. Will open a PR against routing-policy repo.
maria: also let's tune the Grafana alert: current alert fires when aggregate p99 > 800ms for 5m. Change alert to: evaluate on per-shard p99 > 600ms for 3m with an aggregated 'count of impacted shards >= 2' to reduce noisiness.
arun: note on cost tradeoff — lowering the alert threshold may trigger more automated fallbacks to reserved capacity earlier, increasing spend. We should add a budget guard-rail: only escalate to dedicated if estimated token-cost delta < $X/hour or if impacted qps > Y.
j0n: (typo) jon: +1 on budget guard-rail, also add a short-circuit to avoid migrating <1% of traffic.
ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary routing policy updated (PR #823) to include net_retransmit thresholds, canary applied to 5% of traffic in eu-west2.
lee: follow-up items:
- create recording rules (maria/lee)
- update p99 panel to per-shard quantile and change overlay to show tokens/sec and kv-cache hit rate (lee)
- adjust alerting rule thresholds and shard-count logic (jon)
- routing-policy PR to add automated fallback + budget guardrail (arun)
- run a synthetic workload to validate metrics (maria)
maria: i'll own the synthetic run and validate diff between old aggregate query and per-shard quantiles. Will post results here.
jon: thanks — if synthetic shows the false positives go away we should roll out recording rules to prod tomorrow morning during low traffic.
lee: quick snippet to test locally against prometheus: 
```
# compare old vs new approach
old = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
new = max(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by(shard, le)(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])))) by (region)
```
arun: FYI finance asked for an estimate of the extra cost if we auto-fallback for 10% of traffic in eu for 1h. I'll compute and post.
maria: initial synthetic run results (12:40): old-aggregate p99=1.1s, new-per-shard p99=max=260ms, tokens/sec overlay shows a dip during the flap. Looks like aggregation bug + cache warmups explain most of the spike.
jon: great. Filing ops ticket to deploy recording rules and update alerting (OP-621).
lee: will make the Grafana panel change and add tokens/sec and kv-cache hit rate timeseries.
maria: closing loop: increased alert granularity + automations should reduce noisy pages and avoid unnecessary reserved pool migrations. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
